The official added that the two countries’ historical, cultural, and civilizational commonalities, along with the shared will of their leaders, have provided a solid foundation for expanding and deepening bilateral cooperation in various fields.

Pezeshkian further noted that Iran and Kazakhstan, as two important and influential countries in the region, share both the potential and the responsibility to strengthen regional peace, stability, and security.

🎙 Ghalibaf not to attend BRICS parliamentary speakers’ meeting in India

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf will not take part in the 12th meeting of speakers of BRICS parliaments in New Delhi due to “some unforeseen circumstances,” the Iranian Embassy in India has announced.

In a statement posted on its account on X late on Saturday, the embassy said Ghalibaf would be unable to participate in the meeting, scheduled to be held in the Indian capital on October 26-27.
​
The embassy emphasized that an Iranian parliamentary delegation would attend the gathering.
​
“Iran, as one of the members of BRICS, reaffirms its commitment to active and effective participation at the highest levels in the group's summits and meetings,” the statement said.
​
It added that the Iranian delegation would continue its dialogue and consultations with delegations from other member states to expand and deepen bilateral and multilateral cooperation, particularly in parliamentary relations and cooperation.
​
The embassy also expressed its sincere appreciation to the Indian government for hosting the meeting and making the necessary arrangements.
​
It wished the gathering every success, expressing hope that it would produce constructive outcomes to strengthen cooperation and engagement among BRICS members.
​
India is hosting the two-day meeting at the Central Hall of the Samvidhan Sadan complex in Parliament on October 26-27.
​
BRICS is a grouping of emerging economies that includes Iran, which joined the bloc in 2024.
